title: Kusal Mendis ruled out of remaining LPL 2026 matches - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - Colombo Kaps captain Kusal Mendis has been ruled out of the remainder of the Lanka Premier League (LPL) 2026 after sustaining a hamstring injury.

Mendis suffered a right hamstring injury while attempting a run during the Colombo Kaps' match against the Kandy Royals at the SSC Ground in Colombo on July 19.

Following medical assessments, he has been withdrawn from the rest of the tournament and will return to the National High Performance Centre to begin his rehabilitation program.

title: Ex-Australia batter David Warner pleads guilty to drink driving
summary: Former Australia batter David Warner has pleaded guilty to drink driving, after being charged following a random breath test in Sydney in April.

title: Public invited to name Pinnawala Zoo’s three fishing cat cubs - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - As Sri Lanka prepares to celebrate World Cat Day on August 8, Pinnawala Zoo has opened a public naming competition for its three adorable Fishing Cat cubs, inviting animal lovers to suggest creative and meaningful names for the young felines.

The zoo said the best name suggestions will be selected by a judging panel, and the winners will receive special prizes during the World Cat Day celebrations.

Members of the public can submit their ideas through the Google Form shared by Pinnawala Zoo, with entries closing on August 7, 2026.

The zoo has called on families, wildlife enthusiasts and visitors to take part in this special opportunity to become a part of the journey of Sri Lanka’s rare Fishing Cat cubs by helping choose names that match their unique personalities.

title: Ven. Omalpe Sobhitha Thera resigns as Chief Sangha Nayaka - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - Ven. Dr. Omalpe Sobhitha Thera has resigned from the post of Chief Sangha Nayaka of the Southern Province of the Sri Lanka Ramanna Maha Nikaya after serving in the position for 14 years.

His resignation was announced on July 11 at a special meeting of the Southern Province Maha Sangha Sabha held at Sirimangala Piriven Viharaya.

Explaining his decision, Ven. Sobhitha Thera said leadership positions should not be held for life and that opportunities should be given to younger monks to take on responsibilities.

He said Sangha Nayaka positions should not be treated as honorary titles given only in old age, but should be held by those who are able to actively contribute to the development of the Sasana.

Ven. Sobhitha Thera was appointed to the position in 2012 by the Southern Province Sangha Sabha of the Sri Lanka Ramanna Maha Nikaya. Before stepping down, he had handed over responsibilities of 14 temples and educational institutions under his guidance to his disciples and other monks.

title: Some Presidential palaces converted into court houses: PM - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - Some Presidential palaces have been converted into court houses, while others will be used for economically viable purposes, Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya told Parliament today.

Responding to a question raised by MP Chaminda Wijesiri, the Prime Minister said Rs. 13.9 million had been spent on maintaining eight Presidential palaces during 2025 and the first six months of this year.

“The Government has to spend funds to maintain Presidential palaces until they are put to economically viable use,” the Prime Minister added.

title: Veterinarians urge swift passage of Animal Welfare Act - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - The Association of Veterinarians for Humane Management of Animal Population has urged authorities not to further delay the enactment of the Animal Welfare Act, warning that continued delays would prolong the suffering of animals.

Issuing a statement, the association said the Animal Welfare Bill had received Cabinet approval in 2022 and was ready to move forward, but the process was delayed for nearly four years due to objections from certain groups calling for further amendments.

The association noted that the Bill, which has now been gazetted, includes many of the amendments proposed by those groups, and expressed concern over renewed attempts to delay or prevent its passage.

It said the absence of a strong animal welfare law over the past four years had resulted in numerous cases of animals being tortured, abused, and killed, adding that society shares responsibility for the consequences.

“ No bill is perfect. Necessary amendments can be made in the future through the democratic process. However, delaying a law that strengthens animal protection will only extend the suffering of animals,” the association said.

The association called on all parties to support the immediate passage of the Animal Welfare Act, stating that animals have already waited long enough for legal protection.

title: Dengue cases climb to 78,125 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - The number of dengue cases reported in Sri Lanka so far this year has increased to 78,125, according to the latest data released by the National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU).

The NDCU said 1,097 new dengue cases were reported yesterday (21), while 162 Medical Officer of Health (MOH) divisions across the country continue to be identified as high-risk areas for dengue transmission.

Furthermore, a total of 8,590 cases were reported in May, followed by 21,535 cases in June.

During the first 21 days of July alone, 22,749 dengue cases have already been recorded.

The NDCU also confirmed that 56 dengue-related deaths have been reported so far this year, with the case fatality rate standing at 0.07%.

The Western Province continues to account for the highest number of infections, recording 41,236 cases, representing 52.78% of the national total while the Southern Province has reported 11,950 cases (15.30%), while the Central Province has recorded 6,603 cases (8.45%).

title: Southern Province Grade 9 Civic Education exam postponed over question paper delay - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - The Grade 9 Civic Education examination paper scheduled to be held today has been postponed in the Southern Province due to the failure to receive the printed question papers at zonal education offices.

A senior official of the Southern Province Zonal Education told the Daily Mirror that the printing of the question papers had been assigned to a printing company in Kurunegala, but the question paper bundles had not reached examination centres even by yesterday.

As a result, the Southern Province Zonal Education decided not to conduct the examination today and rescheduled it for Friday (July 24).

The official said no incident involving sabotage or leakage of the question paper had been reported.

The Southern Province Zonal Education is expected to conduct an inquiry into the delay in delivering the question papers.

title: Ownership of Water supply and drainage projects under NWSDB to be changed? - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwrdana

Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - Ownership of water supply and drainage projects coming under the purview of the National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) and local bodies are to be changed under the proposed National Water Supply and Drainage Board Amendment Bill which was tabled in Parliament yesterday.

Section 16 of the Bill provides provisions for the NWSDB to take over and carry on any water supply and sewerage undertaking of a local authority, industrial estate, industrial park or community based organisations transferred to the Board by a voluntary transfer order or a compulsory transfer.

Section 17 of the Bill provides provision to the Board to enter into agreements with any person to obtain water from the surface and ground water resources, to engage in activities related to surface and ground water resource development and maintenance of water supply and sewerage services in collaboration with a government department , a person or anybody approved by the subject minister, to set up a subsidiary organisation or a strategic business unit under the provisions of the Companies Act No 7 of 2007 which may in the opinion of the Water Resources Board directly or indirectly promote the interests or be conducive to the attainment of the objects of the Board.

The legislature further makes provisions to take legal action against any party for injury done to the Water Resources Board property and the right to recover the value of any water wasted, misused or unduly consumed.

title: Stop harassing businessmen: Opposition MP - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - The Government has to stop harassing local businessmen, Opposition MP Chamara Sampath Dassanayake said focusing on the arrest of House of Fashion owner whom he revealed has been sent behind bars for undervaluing his assets.

" There are only a handful of Sinhala Buddhist businessmen in this country and they should be safeguarded" the MP told Parliament.

" There is a disturbing trend of harassing businessmen who do not associate with the ruling party. If a businessman associates with either former President Mahinda Rajapaksa or Opposition leader Sajith Premadasa they are arrested and harassed. However, no such action is taken against businessmen who associate with the ruling party" he said.

" Third world countries such as Sri Lanka can never develop when businessmen and entrepreneurs are harassed " he added.

The MP said one cannot be successful if he or she behaves like the current US President Donald Trump who imposes high taxes on nations that oppose him.

Ruling party MP Chandima Hettiarachchi responded and said the Government had nothing to do with the arrest of House of Fashion chief as it is the law enforcement institutions that carried out the operation against him.

title: Dengue threat to continue till mid-August: Health Minister - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - Excepting for three districts, a decreasing trend of the dengue outbreak could be seen in the country.

Claiming that the decreasing trend of the dengue outbreak in the country was due to public concern, Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said yesterday that the risk however will continue for three more weeks until mid August.

He said there is a decreasing trend of dengue cases even in the Colombo District was due to the public being involved.

Responding to a question at the weekly Cabinet briefing, he said the dengue outbreak cannot be controlled by declaring a single day's leave to clean the environment.

He said dengue breeding places could be found in unnoticed places even inside homes as well.

The Minister said the public must get the assistance of the MOH and PHIs to fumigate dengue breeding places until the South West monsoon rains settle.

He said a permanent solution must be found to address the issue after the South West monsoon.

title: France becomes first EU country to ban social media access for under-15s
summary: France’s parliament has approved a bill banning social media access for children under 15, making it the first EU country to bar children from apps such as TikTok.

title: Government undecided over bringing new Constitution: Nalinda - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - Even after nearly two years since the Government came into power, Cabinet spokesman Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said yesterday the Government has still not decided whether to bring in a new Constitution.

He told the weekly Cabinet briefing that however, the Government has ample time to enact a new Constitution within its tenure.

The Minister was responding to a question that the Government promised to abolish the Executive Presidency and bring in a new Constitution and whether the Government is now hoping to go ahead with the amendments.

"We have not decided, as a Government, whether to bring in a New Constitution and what Acts have to be amended. We will reveal it at the right time. Whatever we will do, will be done for the wellbeing of the people," he said.

The Minister said the Constitutional Assembly appointed by previous Governments have met on 82 occasions to discuss about a new Constitution and that there are various opinions about the report of the Constitutional Assembly Steering Committee.

"We can pass a new Constitution within our tenure with the approval of the people. We have obtained the mandate to enact a new Constitution. We need to give an opportunity to the public and discuss it in Parliament for a sufficient time," he said.

Responding to a question that the previous Governments brought in amendments to the Constitution on various occasions for certain purposes and that the Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP) was the first party to come forward against such amendments however, the very party in office now is acting contrary to that and trying to bring in amendment to the Constitution to increase retirement age of the judges, the Minister said the JVP had not always objected to Constitutional amendments and that the party supported the 17th Amendment which introduced independent commissions.

The National People's Power (NPP) promised in its election manifesto to bring in a new Constitution the abolition of the Executive Presidency, expansion of Fundamental Rights, devolution of Power and introduction of Electoral Reforms.

title: Way forward for victims of Microfinance crisis towards recovery - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - Following the recent enactment of the Microfinance and Money Lending Act, the Avanka Lanka Foundation has issued an open letter urging President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to grant special approval for over two million debt-trapped Sri Lankans to form dedicated, village-based Thrift and Credit Cooperative Societies. Writing on behalf of microfinance victims whose government Aswesuma welfare payments are being coerced by predatory lenders, Foundation Chairman Lasantha Mendis called on the President to immediately override a Department of Cooperative Development policy halting new registrations, arguing that specialized, state-backed cooperatives offer the only practical and dignified pathway to rural financial recovery.

Following is the open letter to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake -

The Avanka Lanka Foundation, wishes to congratulate this Government led by the President Anura Kumara Dissanayake on enacting the new Microfinance and the Money Lending Act with the view to protect loan recipients from errant Microfinance providers and money lenders: An achievement that successive Governments were unable to accomplish.

As Your Excellency will know over two million households have been trapped in poverty and over-indebtedness as a result of multiple borrowings from errant microfinance providers who, over many years, targeted financially vulnerable and often financially illiterate women in marginalized rural and urban communities.

Whilst we wholeheartedly welcome the enactment of the new Microfinance and the Money Lending Act, we respectfully wish to bring to your attention the need for a complementary mechanism to protect those who have already fallen victim to these errant microfinance providers whose collection agents coerce borrowers into surrendering a substantial portion of their Aswesuma allowance, thereby depriving these families of the very assistance provided by the Government for their welfare.

In our opinion, one practical and sustainable solution would be to encourage these victims to form Village-Based Thrift and Credit Cooperative Societies, comprising exclusively of affected borrowers of the Microfinance Crisis.

Such societies would provide members with a safe, community-based cooperative society while affording them collective protection from the pressures exerted by collection agents of errant lenders who operate under the guise of microfinance providers.

As the Cooperative Act has an iron clad recovery system, room for wilful defaulters is minimal.

Further, the Department of Cooperative Development could be directed to provide bulk loans to these societies for on-lending to their members to kick start the lending process of the newly formed Cooperative Societies. As members gradually build their savings, these village based Cooperative Societies would become increasingly self-sustaining, enabling the initial funding to be fully recovered with interest over a period of approximately five years.

Unfortunately, this approach cannot be implemented at present because the Department of Cooperative Development has adopted a policy of not registering new Thrift and Credit Cooperative Societies. Consequently, many of the very people whom this Act seeks to protect are left without a practical alternative source of affordable credit, thereby limiting the full effectiveness of this important legislation.

A majority of the victims of the Microfinance crisis are not members of the Cooperative movement for numerous reasons and its not easy for them now to join an existing Cooperative Society and secure adequate amounts of credit to kick start their businesses.

Hence the need for the establishment of dedicated Thrift and Credit Cooperative Societies at village level for Victims of the Microfinance crisis seems to be the need of the hour.

The Cooperative movement has rendered yeoman service in Sri Lanka for over a century and has proven itself despite criticism levelled against them from various quarters.

In view of the above, may we respectfully request you to direct the Minister of Cooperatives to facilitate and encourage the formation of Village-Based Thrift and Credit Cooperative Societies comprising exclusively of victims of the microfinance crisis.

Such an initiative would provide these vulnerable families who have fallen prey to errant Microfinance providers and pave a dignified pathway towards financial recovery.

As mentioned above, the Department of Cooperatives has taken a decision not to register Thrift and Credit Cooperatives.

Hence the appeal to Your Excellency to direct the Minister of Cooperatives to grant special approval to victims of the current Microfinance crisis to form Village based Thrift and Credit Cooperatives.

The Avanka Lanka Foundation is committed to render its assistance on a voluntary basis to implement this initiative be it at beneficiary level or at the level at the Department of Cooperative Development.

We trust you would give this proposal your kind consideration.

We firmly believe that, together with the new Microfinance and Moneylending Act, this initiative would provide a comprehensive and sustainable solution to one of Sri Lanka's most pressing rural socio-economic challenges.

In conclusion we reiterate our gratitude on behalf of the Victims of the Microfinance Crisis and Civil society at large to Your Excellency and your Government for enacting the new Microfinance and Money Lending Act and look forward to Your Excellency's urgent intervention in this regard.

Lasantha Mendis

Founder Chairman

Avanka Lanka Foundation

title: Cruelty accounts for most child abuse cases in Sri Lanka - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - Cruelty has remained the most frequently reported form of child abuse to the National Child Protection Authority (NCPA) over the past 15 years, according to official statistics released by the Department of Census and Statistics.

The data, covering the period from 2010 to 2024, shows that cruelty consistently recorded the highest number of complaints among all categories of child abuse.

Reported cases increased from 905 in 2010 to a peak of 2,741 in 2021 before declining to 1,950 in 2024.

Despite the recent drop, cruelty continued to account for the largest share of complaints received by the NCPA.

Statistics also reveal that non-compulsory education was the second most commonly reported issue, with cases rising from 452 in 2010 to 1,628 in 2024.

Reports relating to lack of care and protection also remained high throughout the years, while complaints of grave sexual abuse, rape and sexual harassment continued to number in the hundreds annually.

According to data, the NCPA also received complaints related to child labour, child marriages, kidnapping, domestic violence, trafficking, juvenile delinquency, online sexual abuse, procuring, soliciting of children and several other forms of abuse and neglect.

Although complaints in some categories have declined in recent years, the figures indicate that thousands of children continue to be affected by abuse, neglect and exploitation each year.
